# BLO-37704 — reap the stale run's pod log when the concurrency guard deletes its Job

Changed files:

- `src/server/execute.ts` — the concurrency guard's stale-Job branch (its run is
  terminal or missing in Paperclip) called `cleanupJob` with **no** `podLogPath`,
  so it deleted the Job and left that run's `.pod.ndjson` on the shared volume.
  It now passes a path rebuilt by a new `podLogPathForForeignJob`.
- `src/server/job-manifest.ts` — `sanitizeForK8sPath` is exported so the
  derivation applies the same transform the path builder does, rather than a
  second copy that can drift.
- `src/server/execute.test.ts` — three cases pinning the branch.

The orphan this leaves belongs to a **different run** than the one executing the
branch, which is why it was worth its own change: the leaked record is someone
else's audit trail, and the run that could have named the file is already gone.

The path is derivable, and that was established by measurement rather than
assumed. A live label read over all 33 running agent Jobs showed every one
carrying company-id, agent-id, run-id, isolation-mode and isolation-key. The
guard's own label selector pins `paperclip.io/agent-id`, so company and agent
are this run's own values — exact, with no label round-trip — and only the run
id and the isolation segment come off the stale Job.

Why the isolation segment keys off the **mode** label and not the presence of the
**key** label, which is the load-bearing detail: those two diverge.
`buildJobManifest` writes both labels whenever `enabled || source === "runtime"`,
but only feeds the key to `buildPodLogPath` when `enabled` — and
`resolveJobIsolation` returns `enabled: false` with a *non-empty* key for a
runtime descriptor whose `isolationMode` is `"shared"`. That shape is live in
production (3 of the 33 Jobs), and for one of them the pod log is demonstrably at
the flat path while no isolated/`agent-shared*` directory has ever existed.
Keying off the key label would have sent the unlink to a path no run ever wrote —
reintroducing the same leak through the obvious fix.

`podLogPathForForeignJob` returns `undefined` when any component is missing, so a
Job created by an older adapter degrades to today's behaviour rather than to a
wrong path. `cleanupJob`'s body, the Job-delete diagnostic, and the
`skipCleanup` / `retainJobs` debug-retention paths are untouched.

Mutation-verified, one mutation per run: dropping the `podLogPath` argument turns
all three new tests red (unlink never called); keying the isolation segment off
the key label turns exactly the shared-mode test red and leaves the other two
green.

No upstream change: this is Paperclip-local code under `src/server/`, not a
carried patch against an upstream adapter release.
